tokens.name: ground
tokens.usage: Default page background. A tinted white in every direction, never pure #ffffff. About 60% of a typical page.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Raised panels, cards, form fields and the email body, on ground.

tokens.name: surface-tint
tokens.usage: Quiet panel fill for grouped content (roster columns, FAQ blocks) on ground.

tokens.name: line
tokens.usage: Hairlines, table rules, card and input borders on ground or surface. Borders separate; shadows are not used.

tokens.name: ink
tokens.usage: Headlines and primary text on ground, surface and surface-tint (12.7:1 or better in all three directions).

tokens.name: ink-body
tokens.usage: Running text and ledes on ground, surface and surface-tint (8.4:1 or better).

tokens.name: ink-muted
tokens.usage: Captions, source lines and metadata on ground, surface and surface-tint (4.7:1 or better).

tokens.name: brand
tokens.usage: The direction's identity hue as a solid field: diagram lines, cover blocks, large graphic areas. Flagship Navy (chosen 6 Oct 2026) keeps today's blue; Podium makes navy the identity; Maple tests a Canadian red.

tokens.name: on-brand
tokens.usage: Text on a brand fill. Flagship: navy on blue is 4.4:1, so large text (24px+) or bold 19px+ only.

tokens.name: action
tokens.usage: Primary button fill and link text on ground and surface (5.0:1 or better).

tokens.name: on-action
tokens.usage: Button labels and icons on an action fill (5.3:1 or better).

tokens.name: lead
tokens.usage: The leadership mark as text: rank numerals, the '11 of 29' proof figure, roster counts. On ground, surface and lead-soft (4.6:1 or better).

tokens.name: lead-fill
tokens.usage: Leadership mark as a solid: the roster count chip, the proof-stat rule, the flagship flag on a jackpot tile.

tokens.name: on-lead-fill
tokens.usage: Text on lead-fill. Flagship pair is 4.4:1: numerals 24px+ only.

tokens.name: lead-soft
tokens.usage: Tinted background behind lead text (proof chips, roster headers).

tokens.name: reward
tokens.usage: Signal: prize values, jackpots, winners, as text on ground, surface and reward-soft (4.7:1 or better). Never buttons or UI chrome. In Podium Gold it shares the lead hue, which is the trade-off of that direction.

tokens.name: reward-fill
tokens.usage: Signal fill for prizes only (a jackpot pip, a winner-story rule). Green and gold together stay under about 6% of a page.

tokens.name: reward-soft
tokens.usage: Tinted background behind reward text.

tokens.name: verified
tokens.usage: Signal: licensed, confirmed, reconciled, as text and icon on ground, surface and verified-soft (5.0:1 or better). Darkened from the identity book's #4e8a1f, which was 3.9:1 on paper. Never a band or background.

tokens.name: verified-fill
tokens.usage: Verified check disc and the completed ledger cell's tick. Graphic only; never carries text.

tokens.name: verified-soft
tokens.usage: Tinted background behind verified text (the licence badge's check area).

tokens.name: error
tokens.usage: Form errors only: error text, the invalid field border and the error summary border, on ground, surface and error-soft (5.7:1 or better). Always paired with words and an icon, never colour alone.

tokens.name: error-soft
tokens.usage: Background of the error summary. Graphic only; text on it uses error or ink.

tokens.name: stage
tokens.usage: Stage band: the dark full-width section that carries heroes, proof and the footer. About 22% of a page.

tokens.name: stage-raised
tokens.usage: Cards and tiles inside a stage band.

tokens.name: stage-line
tokens.usage: Hairlines and tile borders inside a stage band.

tokens.name: on-stage
tokens.usage: Headlines and body text on stage and stage-raised (10:1 or better).

tokens.name: on-stage-muted
tokens.usage: Captions and source lines on stage and stage-raised (5.7:1 or better).

tokens.name: stage-accent
tokens.usage: Eyebrows, links, ghost-button borders and the lead figure on stage (6.3:1 or better on stage and stage-raised).

tokens.name: stage-reward
tokens.usage: Jackpot and prize figures on stage and stage-raised (6.3:1 or better).

tokens.name: stage-verified
tokens.usage: Verified text and the completed ledger cell on stage (8.8:1 or better).

tokens.name: focus
tokens.usage: Keyboard focus ring on light grounds: 2px solid, 2px offset (5:1 or better on ground and surface).

tokens.name: focus-stage
tokens.usage: Keyboard focus ring inside a stage band (6.3:1 or better on stage).

groups.name: Pairing A · Source Serif 4 (considered)
groups.note: Institutional authority. A bookish serif that reads like a hospital foundation's annual report, so the leader claim sounds earned rather than shouted. Pairs with DM Sans body and DM Mono figures.

styles.name: a-h2
styles.sample: 11 of 29 flagships run on our platform

groups.name: Pairing B · Newsreader (chosen)
groups.note: Chosen 6 Oct 2026. Newsroom authority. Tighter and more editorial than A, with optical sizes; reads as 'the record' and suits Raffle Insider. Slightly less warm for grassroots clubs.

styles.name: b-h2
styles.sample: 11 of 29 flagships run on our platform

styles.name: b-h3
styles.usage: Card titles and h3. DM Sans, because the serif is for h1 and h2 only.

groups.name: Pairing C · Libre Franklin
groups.note: Public-institution confidence. A heavy gothic in the tradition of transit signage and newspaper mastheads; the most declarative option. Risk: closer to the SaaS look we are leaving.

styles.name: c-h2
styles.sample: 11 of 29 flagships run on our platform

groups.name: Pairing D · Archivo
groups.note: Scoreboard energy. A grotesk with sports-league heft that speaks to the 30+ sports programs on the platform and the excitement of the draw. Risk: loudest of the four, least gravitas for Tier 1.

styles.name: d-h2
styles.sample: 11 of 29 flagships run on our platform

groups.name: Text · DM Sans
groups.note: Kept from today's site for body and UI in every pairing, so Bricks classes and client-site bases carry over. Load 400, 500 and 700 only.

styles.name: lede
styles.sample: Online, phone, mail and in-person orders, paper and eTickets, on one platform, with a team behind it.

styles.name: body
styles.sample: Every ticket, every channel and every dollar reconciles in one set of books.

styles.name: small
styles.sample: Jackpot figures update from the platform.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Short labels over a figure or field, sentence case. No uppercase, no tracking; set mono only for codes and figures.

groups.name: Figures · DM Mono (chosen)
groups.note: Chosen 6 Oct 2026. The identity book's pick: the mono cut of DM Sans, so body and figures share one voice. Quiet and friendly; a little soft for the big proof figures. Numbers, licence lines and labels in every pairing. Always tabular figures (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums).

styles.name: figure
styles.usage: Ledger cells, jackpot amounts in tiles.

styles.name: figure-lg
styles.usage: The proof stat. One per section.

styles.name: licence
styles.usage: Licence and regulator lines on badges and footers, sentence case. Mono because the licence number is a code.

groups.name: Figures alt · IBM Plex Mono (considered)
groups.note: Engineered and institutional. Crisp, even tabular figures that read as audited numbers, and the steadiest partner for a serif headline. Risk: common in tech products.

groups.name: Figures alt · Martian Mono
groups.note: Wide and square, like a scoreboard or leaderboard. Makes jackpots and the 11 of 29 feel big; pairs with Archivo. Risk: too wide for dense ledgers and long licence lines.

groups.name: Figures alt · Azeret Mono
groups.note: Receipt and ledger precision with distinctive 0 and 1 shapes. Suits reconciliation and every-dollar proof. Risk: the most technical-looking.

groups.name: Figures alt · Courier Prime
groups.note: The printed ticket. Typewriter shapes nod to paper tickets and mail orders, and its email fallback (Courier New) is close. Risk: reads nostalgic rather than leading. Has 400 and 700 only.

groups.name: Figures alt · Red Hat Mono
groups.note: Round and friendly, the warmest option for grassroots clubs. Risk: the softest for Tier 1, and the name carries another brand.

spacing.note: A 4px base with a jump to 72px for section padding, taken from the 2026 identity book.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Icon-to-label gaps.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Inside badges and chips.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Gap between buttons; tile grid gap.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Card inner gaps; minimum page side gutter on phones.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Card padding; desktop side gutter.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Gap between stacked blocks in a section.

tokens.name: space-7
tokens.usage: Section padding on phones; hero column gap.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Section padding on desktop.

shadow.note: Navy-tinted elevation, used sparingly: the page is ground, content sits flat or one step up, and only things that float over other content go higher.

tokens.name: shadow-1
tokens.usage: Resting lift: tiles, badges, cards and dashboard panels on ground.

tokens.name: shadow-2
tokens.usage: Raised: the jackpot or order-summary panel, a strip that overlaps a section edge, button hover.

tokens.name: shadow-3
tokens.usage: Floating: menus, dialogs, sticky bars and presentation frames.

tokens.name: shadow-stage
tokens.usage: Lift for cards inside a stage band, where navy shadows wouldn't show.

radius.note: Firm corners. Pills only for buttons and status chips.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Small boxes, inputs.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Badges, jackpot tiles, roster columns.

tokens.name: radius-lg
tokens.usage: Panels, cards, the stage hero card.

tokens.name: radius-pill
tokens.usage: Buttons and status chips only.
